newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Nelson Hurst.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Nelson Hurst.

text.p: Stockbroker Merrill Lynch singles out London-based insurance broker Nelson Hurst as an attractive investment. The small broker is well placed to take advantage of the niche opportunities presented by recent mergers to create two huge global broking groups.

With 1996 brokerage just topping 50 million stg Nelson Hurst is not in the same league as Aon or Marsh & McLennan. However, during a tough period for brokers, it has achieved steady growth since 1992 when its brokerage was 31.5 million stg.

Much of this growth has come in Latin America and Asia Pacific, both areas with considerable potential. Its strengths in Asia include construction and project insurance, Indonesia and Hong Kong, Merrill Lynch said in a research note.

Clients in Asia Pacific generated 12.6 million stg of brokerage and in Latin America 5.4 million stg last year. Nelson Hurst is the leading reinsurance broker in Venezuela and is progressing well in Brazil, Argentina and Mexico.

The stockbroker's confidence in Nelson Hurst was further boosted by the company's strict cost controls during a period of expansion. Although the headcount rose seven percent to 806, it notes that expenses per head actually fell by one percent.
With its regional strengths and relatively strong broking performance, Merrill Lynch describes Nelson Hurst as one of the best placed brokers.

Nelson Hurst is only one of many insurers interested in Latin America. Chicago based CNA yesterday bought an Argentine insurer, while Swiss Re, itself active in the region, today focused on opportunities in Latin America in its latest Sigma report.
